Aria K.: hey team, first-day hiccup — I'm on Ubuntu 22.04 using OpenConnect (split-tunnel). I can ssh into bastion (10.20.1.5) but `sudo apt update` fails to fetch packages from `apt.internal.redwood` with TLS/SSL errors (certificate signed by unknown authority). Browser to web apps over the bastion via port-forward works. Is the internal CA expected to be installed locally or is there a recommended proxy workaround?
IT Support Bot: (automated) Welcome Aria! For onboarding, you can request temporary network whitelisting by replying with `@IT Support Bot whitelist`. For security-sensitive steps, wait for infra/security ack.
Aria K.: pinging whitelist now: my public IP is 52.45.99.101. I don't want to permanently add CA certs without approval.
Ravi (infra-oncall): welcome Aria. Short answer: we distribute the internal root CA via our endpoint-provisioner for company-managed devices. For BYOD or onboarding we usually do one of two things: 1) add our CA to /usr/local/share/ca-certificates and run `sudo update-ca-certificates` (quick, but persistent), or 2) use an SSH SOCKS proxy so apt/browser fetches go through the bastion and you don't touch system trust. Which are you comfortable with?
Aria K.: prefer not to change system trust on my personal laptop. Can you share the SOCKS approach?
Laila (devops): sure — create a dynamic tunnel from your host (not inside snap/docker) and configure apt to use it. Example: `ssh -f -D 1080 aria@bastion.redwood.internal -N`. Use `socks5h://` so DNS is resolved over the proxy. Then add a small apt config `/etc/apt/apt.conf.d/99socks` (needs sudo):
```
Acquire::http::Proxy "socks5h://localhost:1080";
Acquire::https::Proxy "socks5h://localhost:1080";
```
Then `sudo apt update` should tunnel via bastion and use internal DNS. Note: some SNIs and cert checks still apply but because traffic originates from inside the network it should succeed.
Aria K.: tried that but apt still complains about cert verification for some repos that have internal hostnames. Any special flags?
Dan M. (security): if the repo certs are signed by our internal CA, tunneling alone won't bypass TLS verification — the connection is proxied but the hostname/cert chain still must validate. Usually proxied requests from inside the VPC use certs issued by our PKI that are trusted by our internal CA. If you cannot install the CA, we can instead do a one-off reverse HTTP proxy in the jump host to rewrite certs temporarily, but that's last resort and requires infra approval.
Ravi (infra-oncall): alternative quick unblock: fetch packages from the bastion itself and rsync them, but that's clunky. If you want to avoid touching CA trust, Laila's SOCKS path + a short-lived apt mirror on the bastion works. I'll spin up a temporary http-proxy on the bastion bound to localhost and port-forward it: `ssh -L 3128:127.0.0.1:3128 aria@bastion.redwood.internal -N` then use `Acquire::http::Proxy "http://localhost:3128";` We have squid on bastion but require your IP whitelisted.
Aria K.: I did the SOCKS method but I think apt in a subprocess (like `sudo`) doesn't see my user-local SOCKS. Any tips?
Laila (devops): yep `sudo` drops environment. Two ways: 1) run ssh -D as root (`sudo ssh -f -D 1080 aria@bastion... -N`) or 2) keep the tunnel as your user and use `sudo -E` to preserve env for commands that honor `http_proxy`/`https_proxy`. For apt the explicit `/etc/apt/apt.conf.d/` config is safer because it works system-wide.
Aria K.: ok I created `/etc/apt/apt.conf.d/99socks` and started `ssh -f -D` as my user, then `sudo apt update` still hit cert errors for `packages-internal.redwood` TLS handshake failed.
Dan M. (security): since TLS still failing, we need to either add the internal CA to your trust store or use the bastion-bound http proxy (squid) which has the right trust. Ravi, can you open the proxy and whitelist Aria's session?
deploy-bot: (system) bastion session requested for aria, creating ephemeral squid proxy. audit id: 7f9a2
Ravi (infra-oncall): squid proxy up and bound to localhost:3128 on bastion. I whitelisted your session IP for 2 hours and filed INF-4201 to document onboarding proxy flow. Run: `ssh -L 3128:127.0.0.1:3128 aria@bastion.redwood.internal -N` then set apt proxy to `http://localhost:3128` and retry.
Aria K.: did the port-forward, apt update now works, packages download fine. Thanks! I'll leave the proxy tunnel running while I finish setup.
Laila (devops): pro tip: to make Docker pulls use the proxy, add `export HTTP_PROXY=http://localhost:3128` / `HTTPS_PROXY=...` to your shell or configure in Docker daemon.json if using Docker Desktop.
Aria K.: quick follow-up — is it OK to keep the port-forward running all week while I'm onboarding?
Ravi (infra-oncall): fine for onboarding, keep it <=72 hours. We'll rotate the whitelist and keys after that. If you end up installing the internal root CA (company-managed devices do this automatically), let us know and we'll close the proxy ticket.
Dan M. (security): also note: don't commit internal cert files or keys to Git. If anyone asks you to install a cert, confirm via security channel.
Aria K.: understood, thanks everyone. This unblocked my dev environment. :sparkles:
